key_insight: Spherical Euler–Poisson dynamics in mass coordinates admit a unified analysis of symmetries, conservation laws, collapse expansions and density singularities, with special scaling structure at γ = 4/3.
engineering_relevance: The results provide analytical benchmarks for computational models of self-gravitating gas collapse and numerical detection of shell crossing.
method: Reduce the equations to one radius equation and classify point symmetries and Noether conservation laws.
Construct exact collapse solutions and prove convergent central expansions using the Briot–Bouquet theorem.
Derive surface expansions, singularity criteria and separated linear perturbation modes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computer-algebra checks of all identities and convergence studies of a second-order Lagrangian scheme, including collapse with a free surface.
watch_item: The analysis assumes spherical symmetry and a polytropic gas; extensions to multidimensional flows or more general equations of state are not established here.
paper_title: Symmetries, conservation laws, series solutions and singularity formation for the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations in mass coordinates
